transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-11-11 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (HelixWorks Head of Search), Carlos Ruiz (ML Eng), Sofia Martins (Product), Jared Kim (Eng Manager)

Summary (auto): Quick hosted API walkthrough showing embeddings -> vector store -> rerank flow. Focus on how Redwood Optimize recommends batch sizes, KV/prefix cache, and when to prefer dedicated capacity.

00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll get started in a sec, appreciate you carving out the time.
00:10 Nina Patel: Thanks Maya, excited. We've been poking around the docs but wanted to see the hosted flow end-to-end.
00:20 Maya Chen: Absolutely. I'll do a quick agenda: show embeddings endpoint, the basic similarity search, then the reranker endpoint and how the console Optimize tab suggests config changes. Liam will jump into the demo and the perf numbers.
00:34 Liam O'Connor: Hi folks, quick note on expectations — the demo uses a 100k doc sample and a small reranker model we host for speed, ok if I reference some internal perf numbers?
00:45 Nina Patel: Yes please, we care about tail latency and also cost per query.
00:52 Carlos Ruiz: Also curious about metrics we can export — we use MRR and NDCG primarily.
01:00 Liam O'Connor: Great, we'll show both. So first, embeddings: Redwood's hosted embeddings endpoint returns a 512-d vector by default in this demo. You can change model in the catalog. Call is /v1/embeddings. Response is json array with vectors and token counts.
01:22 Sofia Martins: Quick question — do you do batching automatically? We get bursty traffic.
:01:28 Liam O'Connor: Yes, the runtime does continuous batching; the Console Optimize page will suggest a target batch size and concurrency based on your qps and latency SLO. It tries to balance throughput vs tail.
01:40 Jared Kim: And when would we need Dedicated versus hosted? We're trying to keep costs predictable for a product launch.
01:48 Maya Chen: If you have strict predictable throughput with commit, Dedicated is the go-to. Hosted is easiest to start, and with Optimize you can often meet cost/latency for small-medium workloads. We can show a cost worksheet after.
02:05 Carlos Ruiz: What's the reranker path look like? Do we send the top-K vectors back to rerank model or does Redwood do internal scoring?
02:12 Liam O'Connor: Great question. Typical flow: embeddings -> vector similarity to surface top_k candidates (you choose k) -> call the reranker endpoint with the original query + candidate set. The reranker returns a score for each candidate. You can call the rerank API directly or use the pipeline helper in the SDK.
02:33 Nina Patel: Does reranker support pairwise or listwise training artifacts? We have an existing model trained pairwise.
02:38 Liam O'Connor: The hosted reranker supports both listwise and pointwise scoring. If you have pairwise-trained model weights we can onboard them, or you can use our default reranker. There's also the option to run an ensemble — e.g., lexical boost + neural reranker — which the Console can orchestrate.
03:05 Sofia Martins: Nice. Can you show what the Console Optimize tab recommends for our workload?
03:10 Liam O'Connor: Yep, switching over the Console — okay, here's the Optimize suggestions: batch size 16 for embeddings, top_k 50 for initial retrieval, rerank top_k 10, cache prefix hit ratio expected 0.12, suggested quantization bf16->int8 for the reranker to reduce cost if quality drop is under 0.5% as per your eval set.
03:33 Carlos Ruiz: That quantization note — is that auto-applied or just recommended?
03:38 Liam O'Connor: It's a recommendation. You opt into a quantized variant; Redwood keeps an unquantized fallback. In Dedicated you can pin variants to avoid surprise rollouts.
03:50 Nina Patel: How does prefix or KV cache work in hosted? We have a lot of repeated queries during peak hours.
03:55 Liam O'Connor: We have a few layers: a short-term prefix/KV cache at the serving layer to store recent context completions, and the vector cache for similarity caches. It can reduce per-token compute for repeated contexts. Some customers see 20-40% reduction in token cost depending on hit rate.
04:16 Maya Chen: Quick aside — sometimes transcription reads KV cache as K-V cash in our notes, so apologies if earlier docs had typos.
04:24 Carlos Ruiz: ha, noted.
04:28 Nina Patel: Security: we need SOC 2 and SSO, plus KMS integration. How do hosted options cover KMS?
04:35 Maya Chen: Hosted has envelope encryption with customer KMS integrations for keys and audit logs. We support SAML SSO, RBAC, and can provide COPs level audit exports for dedicated/private. We'll share our security pack.
04:49 Jared Kim: Any concerns about data residency? We're in EMEA and need to keep log copies in region.
04:55 Liam O'Connor: We have region-aware routing; for stricter needs, Private deployment or Dedicated in EU region is available. We'll include region options in the follow-up.
05:08 Sofia Martins: Can you speak to evaluation? We run NDCG@10 and online A/B with interleaving.
05:14 Liam O'Connor: For offline, Redwood's eval suite computes MRR, NDCG@k, precision@k, and delta-lift across prompt sets. The Console can wire up a holdout set and track regressions. For online, we support canary rollouts and traffic splits with automatic fallback if metrics drop.
05:35 Carlos Ruiz: Does Redwood collect per-token cost by route so we can attribute costs to features?
05:40 Maya Chen: Yes, the Console has per-route token cost breakdown, quartiles for latency, and token counts. Great for chargeback across teams.
05:53 Nina Patel: Let's see a live rerank example?
05:58 Liam O'Connor: Sure — I'll run a demo query.
06:02 Liam O'Connor (screen): Running query: "best wireless earbuds for running". Initial retrieval top_5: Document IDs 23, 7, 101, 48, 9. Similarity scores shown but then we pass candidates to reranker.
06:25 Nina Patel: Those ids are fake data set?
06:28 Liam O'Connor: Yep sanitized. Now calling /v1/rerank with payload: query + candidates. Reranker returns new ranking with normalized scores and a confidence score. New top is 7 -> 23 -> 48.
06:45 Carlos Ruiz: Can the reranker output explainability tags? Like which sentence drove the score?
06:50 Liam O'Connor: We have an explain endpoint that returns saliency highlights and token attributions for the candidate snippets, though it adds compute and cost. It's useful for debugging.
07:05 Sofia Martins: Our team cares about latency SLO of p95 < 300ms for storefront queries. Do you see that from hosted?
07:12 Liam O'Connor: For small models and smaller rerankers yes; but p95 depends on sequence length and concurrency. Optimize suggests route rules: a shorter context for storefront, and lower rerank top_k for user-facing queries. If you need strict p95 committed, Dedicated gives a better SLA.
07:33 Nina Patel: Can we do hybrid — hosted for dev and dedicated for prod?
07:37 Maya Chen: Absolutely — that's a common path. We can start hosted for the pilot and bake Dedicated when you hit commit thresholds.
07:45 Jared Kim: How do you handle scoring tie-breakers between lexical and semantic?
07:50 Liam O'Connor: The Console supports a scoring lambda where you can blend BM25 score with semantic score — configurable weight and we surface calibration tools for a small eval set.
08:07 Carlos Ruiz: If we rely on our in-house BM25, can Redwood call our service in the pipeline?
08:13 Liam O'Connor: Yes, pipeline hooks allow you to call external ranking signals; we can stitch it into the rerank request.
08:20 Nina Patel: Any limits on candidate size for reranker? We have candidates with long snippets sometimes up to 4,000 chars.
08:27 Liam O'Connor: Sequence length affects latency and memory; we'll show a suggested truncation and snippet extraction strategy. For long docs, we prefer snippet extraction or chunking and reranking at snippet level.
08:40 Sofia Martins: Show me the Optimize cost tradeoff screen again.
08:44 Liam O'Connor (screen): Here's the estimated cost delta chart — moving reranker to int8 quantized variant reduces per-rerank cost by ~40% at a predicted NDCG drop of 0.3 points. Batch sizes and cache hit also shown.
09:05 Carlos Ruiz: Hmm 40% is tempting. How do you validate the NDCG drop can't be worse in our data?
09:12 Liam O'Connor: We run a quantization validation on your held-out set and report delta MRR/NDCG. We recommend running a small pilot on live traffic with canary rollout to verify.
09:25 Nina Patel: On the SDK side, what's the cutter for retry/backoff? We get occasional 503s during GC windows.
09:31 Maya Chen: SDK includes exponential backoff with jitter; Console shows error heatmaps so we can correlate with infra events. For Dedicated, those GC windows are minimized.
09:45 Carlos Ruiz: Do you export raw logs for us to pipe into our ELK stack?
09:50 Liam O'Connor: Yes, we support log sinks to your S3 or SIEM; you can stream audit logs and request traces.
09:58 Sofia Martins: Any gotchas with rate limits?
10:01 Maya Chen: Hosted has soft rate limits; we can raise them during pilot. Dedicated gives hard dedicated throughput.
10:08 Nina Patel: Can we do offline reranking with batch jobs instead of real-time? We have nightly enrichment pipelines.
10:13 Liam O'Connor: Yes, batch rerank is supported. You can call the rerank endpoint in bulk or use the private batch runner in Dedicated.
10:20 Jared Kim: We might need a hybrid: offline re-rank nightly and online top-K rerank for freshness.
10:25 Maya Chen: That is common and works well.
10:28 Carlos Ruiz: Back to metrics — you mentioned automatic regression alerts. How are those triggered?
10:33 Liam O'Connor: The Console watches evaluation sets and live metrics; you set guardrails on MRR/NDCG delta thresholds and we'll alert and auto-rollback if they exceed tolerances.
10:45 Nina Patel: Great. What's the expected turnaround to get a pilot running end-to-end? We can supply sample data quickly.
10:50 Maya Chen: If you provide sample queries and a ground-truth CSV, we can spin a hosted pilot in about 5 business days: onboarding + run initial eval. Dedicated takes longer due to capacity provisioning.
11:04 Carlos Ruiz: Any compliance paperwork? We'll loop in Security.
11:08 Maya Chen: We'll share the security pack and SOC2 artifacts; we can arrange an SSO/KMS tech session with Security next week.
11:18 Sofia Martins: Perfect. Can you recap the pilot scope?
11:21 Maya Chen: Yes — Pilot scope: hosted API, embeddings->vector store->rerank pipeline on a 5k-50k doc sample, measure MRR/NDCG, tune top_k and quantization, run 2-week live canary. Deliverables: cost worksheet, security pack, sample eval scripts, pilot kickoff calendar invite.
11:45 Nina Patel: That sounds good. One last question: do you provide pre-built connectors to common vector stores? We use a managed vector DB for ML infra.
11:52 Liam O'Connor: We have connectors and SDK helpers for Pinecone, Milvus, and S3-backed indices; we can adapt to your managed store.
12:03 Carlos Ruiz: Okay, let's move forward. I'll upload the sample dataset by EOD Monday.
12:08 Maya Chen: Awesome — we'll follow up with materials and schedule the pilot kickoff. Thanks everyone.
12:15 Nina Patel: Thanks, this was helpful.
12:20 Meeting end.
